companyDescription: AI Semiconductors + Infrastructure Software · Custom AI XPUs for hyperscalers (Google TPU, Meta, OpenAI Jalapeño) + VMware enterprise software
priceNote: Still absorbing Jun 3 Q2 guidance miss (-13-15% that day) — down ~26% from 52-week high $495; today's -2.2% is broader AI-chip demand-slowdown sentiment, not new AVGO-specific news
summary: Broadcom sold off ~26% from its high after Q2 FY26 earnings (Jun 3): EPS beat ($2.44 vs $2.40 est) but Q3 AI chip guidance of $16B missed the $17.2B Street estimate, and management didn't raise the full-year $100B AI semiconductor target — a sell-the-news reaction that dragged the whole SOX index down. Since then, the OpenAI 'Jalapeño' custom inference chip unveiling (Jun 24) reinforced the 10GW multi-year custom silicon partnership through 2029. With consensus analyst target near $500 (+35% from here) and Buy ratings from 26+ analysts, the pullback looks like a guidance-driven reset rather than a broken thesis — but Q3 earnings (Sep 3) is the next real confirmation point.

catalysts.name: Q3 FY2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: First earnings since the Jun 3 guidance miss. Market will watch whether the $16B AI chip guide was conservative sandbagging or a real demand air-pocket, and whether management finally raises the full-year $100B AI semis target.

catalysts.name: OpenAI Jalapeño Chip — Initial Deployment
catalysts.description: Custom LLM-inference ASIC unveiled Jun 24, 2026 as part of the 10GW OpenAI-Broadcom accelerator partnership (through 2029). Initial deployment targeted by end of 2026 — a concrete milestone for the custom silicon TAM story.

catalysts.name: VMware Software Integration / Margin Ramp
catalysts.description: Infrastructure software (VMware) is the highest-margin segment; Q2 software revenue growth disappointed and was the other leg of the Jun 3 sell-off alongside AI guidance. Watch for re-acceleration as private-cloud migrations mature.

catalysts.name: Hyperscaler Custom XPU Demand (Google, Meta, new customers)
catalysts.description: Broadcom's custom AI accelerator (XPU) business depends on continued hyperscaler capex. Any signs of AI capex deceleration from Google/Meta/ByteDance earnings calls in H2 2026 would pressure the multi-year AI semis growth forecast (~40%/yr through FY29).

risks: Q3 AI chip guidance ($16B) missed Street est. ($17.2B) — first crack in the 'always beat and raise' AI narrative
Management held full-year $100B AI semis target flat rather than raising it — reads as caution after 3 straight raises
P/E ~63x still prices in a lot of AI growth; any second consecutive guide-down would compress the multiple hard
VMware/software growth disappointed in Q2 — the highest-margin segment showing early softness
SOX-wide 'buyer exhaustion' concern — sell-off spread to Intel, AMD, Micron, Marvell, suggesting a sector re-rating risk, not just AVGO-specific
Hawkish Fed tilt (median dot raised to 3.8% for 2026, hike risk flagged by Warsh) pressures long-duration AI-capex multiples
Customer concentration — Google, Meta, and now OpenAI represent outsized share of custom silicon revenue; any one program delay/slowdown moves the stock

estimateDates.note: Key test: did $16B AI chip guide hold, and does mgmt finally raise the $100B FY26 AI semis target
First racks of OpenAI custom inference chip go live — proof point for the 10GW multi-year deal

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held 3.50–3.75% for a 4th straight meeting on Jun 17, 2026 under new Chair Kevin Warsh. Next FOMC Jul 28–29. Updated dot plot raised the 2026 median projection to 3.8% — 9 of 19 officials see at least one more hike this year, a hawkish surprise vs prior cut expectations.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation still running above the 2% target, partly on energy-related supply shocks. Warsh reiterated price stability as the primary objective at the ECB Sintra forum, signaling no near-term dovish pivot.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: High-P/E AI/semis names like AVGO (~63x) are the most rate-sensitive part of the market — a hawkish surprise compresses long-duration growth multiples faster than it hits earnings. This adds to the guidance-miss overhang rather than offsetting it.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — no imminent hike, but the dot-plot shift toward tightening removes a tailwind AI stocks had been pricing in, layering macro risk on top of the Jun 3 guidance disappointment.

entryStrategy.verdict: BUY the guidance-miss reset — Q2 beat on EPS, Jalapeño deal validates the custom silicon TAM, and consensus target implies +35% upside. Scale in now with the bulk of size reserved for a dip toward $335-350 pre-Q3 earnings (Sep 3).

catalystSpot.preRunup: AVGO has historically run up 5-10% in the weeks before earnings on AI-cycle optimism, but the Jun 3, 2026 print broke that pattern — guidance miss triggered an immediate post-earnings selloff instead. Going into Sep 3, expect a more cautious pre-earnings drift given the recent guide-down.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 1–2 weeks pre-earnings (historical norm, muted this cycle)

postWin.note: Dec 2024 (FY24 Q4) earnings: AVGO jumped ~15% after-hours on strong AI revenue growth forecast and raised medium-term AI guidance — the clearest comparable 'good' AI-guidance reaction in this stock's history.

postLose.note: Jun 3, 2026 (Q2 FY26): stock fell ~13-15% intraday after AI chip guidance ($16B) missed the $17.2B Street estimate and management held the full-year $100B AI target flat instead of raising it — this is the direct, most recent comparable.

spotSizing.reason: BUY verdict with a dated, high-clarity catalyst (Sep 3 earnings) and +35% consensus upside, but the Jun 2026 guidance miss shows real event risk in this name now — size at 5% initial, add on dip to $335-350 pre-earnings rather than sizing up fully at current price.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below post-Jun 3 earnings support — thesis would need re-underwriting

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Sep 3 AI chip guidance misses again AND the $100B full-year target is cut (not just held flat), exit — that would be a genuine demand-slowdown signal, not just conservative guidance
